status: WRITTEN candidates with WRITTEN-checked-in-kernel exact finite replays; not parent adoption
primary_finding: An explicit compact CONVEX polytope of monic Hurwitz septics has globally separated, alternating parity-root bands, all five required strict-certificate phase/ratio features, and an exact strictly-negative eight-coordinate five-atom sum normalized to (-1,...,-1,-1256521167/64000000). Hence no common equal-degree SPR numerator exists for that stable polytope. However its independent coefficient interval hull contains s^7+700s^6+(25/2)s^5+s^4+46s^3+10000s^2+29s+1, with H3=-15531251, so every interval box containing the vertices is ineligible. This proves that compact convex stability and separated common root bands alone cannot imply a universal positive answer; any positive proof must use independent coefficient-box structure.
supporting_findings: A strict ratio necessary condition for five-node strict certificates holds on an actual eligible box, but the box's common numerator gives positive pairings on all five atoms; the condition is not sufficient.

A separate five-atom negative sum for individually stable real-rooted septics violates common root-band ordering and has unstable convex/interval hulls; it is an even weaker ineligible countermechanism.
remaining_gap: No ORIGINAL eligible independent interval box with a strict negative certificate, and no universal positive theorem, is established. The convex polytope counterexample identifies the missing ingredient but is not itself a counterexample to the original problem.
next_action: Search for an interval-box-preserving modification of the stable-polytope negative mechanism, using actual corner atoms and endpoint-independent constraints.
